tagline: Salt ponds and farm landmarks along an old mail corridor.
intro: Route 1 through South Kingstown passes farmland, marinas and woods south of the Wakefield cutoff, with houses and businesses along its northern section. Designated a Rhode Island scenic roadway in May 2018, it includes 12.35 miles within South Kingstown; the half-mile passage through Narragansett is excluded. RIDOT highlights salt-pond views and approximately four miles of roadside stone walls. Deciduous and coniferous woods mix with shrubs beside the highway. On clear days, views extend across Narragansett Bay to Aquidneck Island and Newport.

The corridor developed from Indigenous trails into a colonial route carrying mail and newspapers. The numbered highway does not simply preserve that earlier road: portions follow the Boston Post Road, while bypasses left other sections as US 1A. The town’s stewardship committee was charged with protecting the corridor’s historic and scenic qualities while recognizing its role as a transportation route.

Traveling north from Charlestown, the route reaches Moonstone Beach Road, then the junctions for Ministerial Road and Matunuck Beach Road. Willow Dell stands just west of Matunuck Beach Road, and Point Judith Pond is visible from Route 1. The highway becomes a freeway by Wakefield, then returns to surface-road junctions before reaching the Hannah Robinson Tower at Route 138 and continuing toward North Kingstown.

moments.title: Willow Dell
moments.text: A stone marker beside the highway identifies the Wager Weeden Memorial Fountain at Willow Dell, just west of Matunuck Beach Road. The farmhouse predates the Weeden family: Colonel Jeremiah Bowen built its main block circa 1752, and Wager Weeden bought it in 1826. His descendants still own the property. The seven-acre parcel includes two barns, a garage and a former stable converted to housing. The house has a gambrel roof, and it entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1996. Willow Dell also carries the name Weeden Farm, retaining the family association in the property’s name.
moments.notice: The Wager Weeden Memorial Fountain is marked by a stone beside the south side of the highway.

moments.title: Point Judith Pond
moments.text: Point Judith Pond lies behind barrier beaches and dunes, a shallow salt pond four miles long. Route 1 offers a view of the pond. A narrow passage through the shoreline connects it to Point Judith Harbor; fishing vessels and recreational boats use this waterway. Harbor works began in 1905, and three stone breakwaters were built in 1914. Inside the pond, a 4.5-mile channel follows its western side to Wakefield, carrying the engineered waterway inland beyond the harbor entrance. The pond itself forms part of the boundary between Narragansett and South Kingstown.

moments.title: Hannah Robinson Tower
moments.text: The tower at Route 138 was rebuilt using the earlier structure’s pillars. The Civilian Conservation Corps built a tower here in 1938; it served as an observation tower during World War II. The 1988 rebuilding reused those pillars, and the tower now stands 40 feet high. Its name commemorates Hannah Robinson, who lived from 1746 to 1773. RIDOT identifies both the observation tower and Hannah Robinson Rock at the Route 138 intersection. The state maintains the land as a memorial to Hannah Robinson, with the nearby rock included in the preserved area.
